ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: Science and democracy share important principles and ideals that oppose illegitimate claims for knowledge and power. The authority of both scientific knowledge and democratic governance is legitimated by representation. It is only when this representation is accepted as legitimate that it can support the authority of the knowledge claims made, or the authority of particular forms of governance. Representation is, however, never perfect or complete. Since both scientific practices and democratic governance, in principle, admit potential alternative representations, continuous struggles over what is represented and what is not can be foreseen. To represent means to simplify, which implies the existence of alternatives — alternative ways of simplifying complicated issues. This further means that both science and democracy have inbuilt mechanisms for improvement, which are based on critical assessments of existing representations.

questions.passage: Science and democracy ①<u>share</u> important principles and ideals that oppose illegitimate claims for knowledge and power. The authority of both scientific knowledge and democratic governance is ②<u>legitimating</u> by representation. It is only when this representation is ③<u>accepted</u> as legitimate that it can support the authority of the knowledge claims made, or the authority of particular forms of governance. Representation is, however, never perfect or complete. Since both scientific practices and democratic governance, in principle, admit potential alternative representations, continuous struggles over what is represented and what is not can be ④<u>foreseen</u>. To represent means to simplify, which implies the existence of alternatives — alternative ways of simplifying complicated issues. This further means that both science and democracy have inbuilt mechanisms for improvement, which are based on critical assessments of existing representations.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② legitimating → legitimated: 'The authority ... is legitimated by representation'에서 주어 authority가 정당화되는 것이므로 수동태(is legitimated)가 필요. legitimating(능동형 현재분사)은 부적절
det.analysis:
✅ ① share: 'Science and democracy share important principles'에서 복수 주어(Science and democracy)에 호응하는 복수 동사로 올바른 어법
❌ ② legitimating → legitimated: 'The authority ... is legitimating by representation'에서 be + p.p. 수동태 구조가 필요. 권위가 대표에 의해 '정당화되는(legitimated)' 것이므로 과거분사가 올바름. 현재분사 legitimating은 부적절 ←정답
✅ ③ accepted: 'this representation is accepted as legitimate'에서 수동태(is accepted) 구조로 올바른 어법
✅ ④ foreseen: 'continuous struggles ... can be foreseen'에서 조동사 + be + p.p. 수동태 구조로 올바른 어법
det.tip: 'The authority is legitimated by representation'에서 권위는 대표에 의해 정당화'되는' 것이므로 수동태(be + p.p.)가 필요합니다. legitimating(현재분사)은 능동의 의미이므로 부적절합니다.

questions.passage: Science and democracy share important principles and ideals ①<u>that</u> oppose illegitimate claims for knowledge and power. The authority of both scientific knowledge and democratic governance is legitimated by representation. It is only when this representation is accepted as legitimate that it can support the authority of the knowledge claims made, or the authority of ②<u>particular</u> forms of governance. Representation is, however, never perfect or complete. Since both scientific practices and democratic governance, in principle, admit potential alternative representations, continuous struggles over what is ③<u>representing</u> and what is not can be foreseen. To represent means to simplify, which implies the existence of alternatives — alternative ways of ④<u>simplifying</u> complicated issues. This further means that both science and democracy have inbuilt mechanisms for improvement, which are based on critical assessments of existing representations.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ representing → represented: 'what is represented and what is not'에서 수동태(be represented)가 필요. 대표'되는' 것이므로 과거분사 represented가 올바름
det.analysis:
✅ ① that: 'ideals that oppose illegitimate claims'에서 선행사 ideals를 수식하는 주격 관계대명사로 올바른 어법
✅ ② particular: 'the authority of particular forms'에서 명사 forms를 수식하는 형용사로 올바른 어법
❌ ③ representing → represented: 'what is representing and what is not'에서 '대표되는 것(what is represented)'이라는 수동 의미이므로 과거분사 represented가 필요. 현재분사 representing은 능동 의미이므로 부적절 ←정답
✅ ④ simplifying: 'alternative ways of simplifying complicated issues'에서 전치사 of 뒤 동명사로 올바른 어법
det.tip: 'what is represented'는 '대표되는 것'이라는 수동 의미입니다. representing(능동)으로 바꾸면 '대표하고 있는 것'이 되어 문맥과 맞지 않습니다.

questions.passage: Science and democracy share important principles and ideals that oppose illegitimate claims for knowledge and power. The authority of both scientific knowledge and democratic governance is legitimated by representation. ①<u>What</u> is only when this representation is accepted as legitimate that it can support the authority of the knowledge claims ②<u>made</u>, or the authority of particular forms of governance. Representation is, however, never perfect or complete. Since both scientific practices and democratic governance, in principle, admit potential alternative representations, continuous struggles over what is represented and what is not can be foreseen. To represent ③<u>means</u> to simplify, which implies the existence of alternatives — alternative ways of simplifying complicated issues. This further means that both science and democracy have inbuilt mechanisms for improvement, which are ④<u>based</u> on critical assessments of existing representations.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ① What → It: 'It is only when this representation is accepted ... that it can support ...'에서 It is ~ that 강조구문. What으로 시작하면 구문이 성립하지 않음
det.analysis:
❌ ① What → It: 'What is only when this representation is accepted as legitimate that it can support'에서 It is ~ that 강조구문의 가주어 It이 필요. What으로 시작하면 that절과 호응하지 않아 비문 ←정답
✅ ② made: 'the knowledge claims made'에서 과거분사가 claims를 후치 수식하는 구조로 올바른 어법
✅ ③ means: 'To represent means to simplify'에서 To부정사 주어는 단수 취급, 3인칭 단수 동사 means 올바른 어법
✅ ④ based: 'which are based on critical assessments'에서 수동태(be based on) 구조로 올바른 어법
det.tip: 'It is only when ... that ~'는 강조구문입니다. 가주어 It이 필요하며, What으로 시작하면 that절과 호응하지 않아 구문이 성립하지 않습니다.

questions.passage: Science and democracy share important principles and ideals that ①<u>oppose</u> illegitimate claims for knowledge and power. The authority of both scientific knowledge and democratic governance is legitimated by representation. It is only when this representation is accepted as ②<u>legitimate</u> that it can support the authority of the knowledge claims made, or the authority of particular forms of governance. Representation is, however, never perfect or complete. Since both scientific practices and democratic governance, in principle, admit potential alternative representations, continuous struggles over what is represented and what is not can be foreseen. To represent means to ③<u>simplify</u>, which implies the existence of alternatives — alternative ways of simplifying complicated issues. This further means that both science and democracy have inbuilt mechanisms for ④<u>stagnation</u>, which are based on critical assessments of existing representations.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ stagnation(정체) → improvement(향상): 과학과 민주주의가 향상(improvement)을 위한 내재된 메커니즘을 가진다는 문맥에서 stagnation(정체)은 정반대
det.analysis:
✅ ① oppose(반대하다): 부당한 주장에 반대한다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ② legitimate(정당한): 대표가 정당한 것으로 받아들여진다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ③ simplify(단순화하다): 대표한다는 것은 단순화한다는 것을 의미한다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ④ stagnation → improvement: 'both science and democracy have inbuilt mechanisms for stagnation'에서 원문은 '향상(improvement)을 위한 메커니즘'인데 stagnation(정체)은 정반대 ←정답
det.tip: 과학과 민주주의는 비판적 평가에 기반한 향상(improvement)을 위한 내재된 메커니즘을 가집니다. stagnation(정체)은 정반대 의미입니다.

questions.passage: Science and democracy share important principles and ideals that oppose illegitimate claims for knowledge and power. The ①<u>authority</u> of both scientific knowledge and democratic governance is legitimated by representation. It is only when this representation is accepted as legitimate that it can support the authority of the knowledge claims made, or the authority of particular forms of governance. Representation is, however, never perfect or complete. Since both scientific practices and democratic governance, in principle, ②<u>deny</u> potential alternative representations, continuous struggles over what is represented and what is not can be foreseen. To represent means to simplify, which implies the existence of ③<u>alternatives</u> — alternative ways of simplifying complicated issues. This further means that both science and democracy have inbuilt mechanisms for improvement, which are based on ④<u>critical</u> assessments of existing representations.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② deny(부정하다) → admit(인정하다): 과학적 실천과 민주적 거버넌스가 잠재적 대안적 대표를 '인정한다(admit)'는 문맥에서 deny(부정하다)는 정반대
det.analysis:
✅ ① authority(권위): 과학적 지식과 민주적 거버넌스의 권위가 대표에 의해 정당화된다는 문맥에 적절
❌ ② deny → admit: 'both scientific practices and democratic governance ... deny potential alternative representations'에서 원문은 잠재적 대안적 대표를 '인정한다(admit)'인데 deny(부정하다)는 정반대 ←정답
✅ ③ alternatives(대안들): 대안의 존재를 함의한다는 문맥에 적절
✅ ④ critical(비판적인): 기존 대표에 대한 비판적 평가에 기반한다는 문맥에 적절
det.tip: 과학과 민주주의는 원칙적으로 잠재적 대안적 대표를 인정합니다(admit). deny(부정하다)는 정반대 의미입니다.

The authority of both scientific knowledge and democratic governance is legitimated by representation. It is only when this representation is accepted as __________ that it can support the authority of the knowledge claims made, or the authority of particular forms of governance. Representation is, however, never perfect or complete. Since both scientific practices and democratic governance, in principle, admit potential alternative representations, continuous struggles over what is represented and what is not can be foreseen. To represent means to simplify, which implies the existence of alternatives — alternative ways of simplifying complicated issues. This further means that both science and democracy have inbuilt mechanisms for improvement, which are based on critical assessments of existing representations.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 대표가 '정당한(legitimate)' 것으로 받아들여질 때에야 지식 주장의 권위를 뒷받침할 수 있다는 문맥
det.analysis:
✅ ① legitimate: 'this representation is accepted as ____'에서 대표가 '정당한(legitimate)' 것으로 받아들여져야 권위를 뒷받침한다는 원문에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② alternative: '대안적인(alternative)' 것으로 받아들여진다는 것은 문맥상 권위 뒷받침과 어울리지 않음. 대안적 대표는 오히려 기존 대표에 대한 도전
❌ ③ complicated: '복잡한(complicated)' 것으로 받아들여진다는 것은 권위 정당화와 무관
❌ ④ particular: '특정한(particular)' 것으로 받아들여진다는 것은 정당화와 직접 연결되지 않음
det.tip: 대표가 정당한(legitimate) 것으로 받아들여질 때에야 비로소 지식 주장이나 거버넌스의 권위를 뒷받침할 수 있습니다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 대표하는 것은 단순화하는 것을 의미하며, 이는 '대안의 존재(the existence of alternatives)'를 함의한다
det.analysis:
✅ ① the existence of alternatives: 'To represent means to simplify, which implies ____'에서 단순화는 곧 대안이 존재함을 의미한다는 원문에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② the authority of particular forms: 본문에 등장하는 표현이지만, 단순화가 '특정 형태의 권위'를 함의한다는 것은 논리적으로 맞지 않음. 권위는 대표에 의해 정당화되는 것
❌ ③ continuous struggles over what is represented: 본문에 등장하지만, 투쟁은 대표의 불완전성에서 비롯되는 결과이지, 단순화가 직접 함의하는 것이 아님
❌ ④ critical assessments of existing representations: 본문에 등장하지만, 비판적 평가는 향상 메커니즘의 기반이지, 단순화가 함의하는 것이 아님
det.tip: 대표한다는 것은 단순화한다는 것이며, 이는 대안의 존재(the existence of alternatives)를 함의합니다.
